_what: H3 for the filter grammar (#896 task 2): every group of phrases on which packages/tagger/src/grammar/filter.ts and parseSubject disagree, grouped by the SubjectFilter fields that differ, over packages/tagger/phrases.jsonl. Each group is labelled after reading EVERY member, not a sample. 'grammar right' cites the rule or the printed text; 'grammar wrong' must be fixed before task 3 switches derive over; 'both wrong' says what neither reads. phrase-diff-triage.test.ts fails when a group appears, disappears or changes size, and when the parsed count moves, so a change to either parser is re-triaged and banked here.

control.label: grammar right
control.why: Two shapes, both right. (1) 'spells you cast' (70 of 73): a spell's controller is the player who put it on the stack, so the caster is the controller -- parseSubject's control regex knows 'you control' and 'your' but not 'you cast', and answered any. (2) 'of an opponent's choice' / 'of your choice' (6): the chooser is not the controller; parseSubject read 'opponent'/'your' anywhere and answered opp/you. A Clue, Food or Treasure 'of your choice' is created under the creator's control by CONTROLLER_DEFAULT, not by this word. The 'that targets only' member names the TARGET's controller, not the spell's, and the subject is refused (restricted) either way. 'a token that's a copy of a permanent you control': 'you control' names the ORIGINAL, not the token, which CONTROLLER_DEFAULT gives its creator (CR 111.2).

scope.label: grammar right
scope.why: (1) 'creatures target player controls', 'a creature target opponent controls': the player is the target, the creatures are not -- parseSubject's scope reads 'target' anywhere in the string. (2) 'any number of targets', 'one or two targets': parseSubject's \btarget\b misses the plural. (3) 'a creature each opponent controls': the quantifier binds the opponent. (4) Two token names ('Kobolds of Kher Keep', 'Llanowar Elves'): a plural in a NAME is not a mass subject. (5) 'a token that's a copy of target creature': the original is targeted, the token is created, not targeted. Copy tokens of a target ('a token that's a copy of target artifact') are not themselves targeted.

fromZone,scope.label: grammar right
fromZone,scope.why: 'a nonland card from target opponent's hand' (Thoughtseize family): the target is the opponent, not the card, and the card comes from a hand. parseSubject's ORIGIN_ZONE allows only a|an|your|their|the before the zone, so a possessive player ('target opponent's', 'each opponent's') drops the zone, and its scope reads the player's 'target'.

other.label: grammar right
other.why: 'up to one other target creature', 'one or more other creatures', 'any number of other permanents': 'other' after a count. parseSubject's `other` regex accepts at most one word before it. Also 'target creature other than this creature', 'all creatures other than this creature': the same fact as 'another' written out.

fromZone.label: grammar right
fromZone.why: 'target card from an opponent's graveyard', '... from defending player's graveyard': the same ORIGIN_ZONE possessive gap as the fromZone,scope group, where the possessive carries no 'target'. Also 'lands from the top of your library' and 'creature spells from the top of your library' (Courser/Future Sight family: the origin is the library), and 'up to two target cards from a single graveyard' / 'from graveyards' / 'from all graveyards' (the cards come from a graveyard; 'single' constrains how many graveyards, not the class). parseSubject's ORIGIN_ZONE reads none of these.

zone.label: grammar right
zone.why: 'target creature card in your graveyard', 'all cards in your hand': `zone` is where the subject lives and absent means the battlefield (schema), so parseSubject's reading puts every one of these on the battlefield. TASK 3 CAUTION: on a producer, zone graveyard is read as a graveyard FILL by graveyardFillMatches; the switch must check each consumer of `zone` before trusting this field from the grammar. The two OR-lists whose alternatives have different heads ('target spell, nonland permanent, or card in a graveyard', 'an artifact or a card in your hand') are refused, not zoned. Also 'Enchant creature card in a graveyard' (Animate Dead's enchant line, CR 303.4a) and 'cards in graveyards' (plural).

owner.label: grammar right
owner.why: 'target creature you own', 'Commander creatures you own': ownership is a stated fact the schema has a field for (`owner`, Zedruu #681); parseSubject never sets it from 'you own'.

named.label: grammar right
named.why: 'a 1/2 blue Bird creature token with flying named Storm Crow': the name belongs to the token being created (G2b ruling, 2026-08-21). parseSubject's TOKEN_CREATION wants 'token named' adjacent, so a 'with flying' between them made it read a card name to look for.

subtype.label: grammar right
subtype.why: Words inside a NAME or a COUNTER KIND are not subtypes: 'a card named Forest', 'Scion of Darkness', 'Kobolds of Kher Keep', 'Cloud Sprite', 'a creature with a fungus counter on it', 'a land with a mine counter on it'. parseSubject's subtype sweep reads every word; the grammar reads the name and the counter as what they are. The 'that targets only a single Golem' member is refused (restricted) either way.

anyOf,subtype,type.label: grammar right
anyOf,subtype,type.why: 'all creatures and Vehicles', 'an Aura, creature, or planeswalker card', 'target Spirit, instant, or sorcery card': a type on one side and a subtype on the other is an OR across slots. parseSubject's crossSlotOr splits on 'or' only, so 'and' lists and comma lists whose first piece holds both a type and a subtype were read as type AND subtype -- a Vehicle that must also be a creature.

type.label: grammar right
type.why: 'an instant or sorcery spell that targets only this creature': the type is the spell's; 'creature' is what it targets. Refused (restricted) either way, so no claim moves.

control,type.label: grammar right
control,type.why: 'a spell that targets only a single creature you control': type and control both belong to the target in the relative clause, not to the spell. Refused (restricted) either way.

notType,type.label: grammar right
notType,type.why: 'a non-creature card from your graveyard': hyphenated. parseSubject's \bcreature\b matches inside 'non-creature', the negation then removes the only type, and it falls through to type creature -- the inverse of the text.

scope,zone.label: grammar right
scope,zone.why: 'each card in target opponent's hand': the player is targeted and the cards live in a hand.

allTypes,anyOf,subtype,type.label: grammar right
allTypes,anyOf,subtype,type.why: 'Artifact creatures and Heroes you control': an artifact creature OR a Hero; parseSubject demanded an artifact creature Hero.

combat.label: grammar right
combat.why: 'attacking player' is a player, not an attacking creature. 'target attacking or blocking creature' (13 phrases, 87 card uses) is `in-combat` (CR 506.4): parseSubject read only 'attacking'.

named,subtype.label: grammar right
named,subtype.why: 'a 3/1 colorless Wall artifact creature token with defender named Stone Boulder': the token's own name, and 'stone' is not a subtype of it.

owner,zone.label: grammar right
owner,zone.why: 'a card you own in exile with a study counter on it': owned by you, in exile.

subtype,type.label: grammar right
subtype,type.why: 'a colorless artifact token named Land Mine': an artifact token; 'Land' and 'Mine' are its name.

type,umbrella.label: grammar right
type,umbrella.why: 'target spell that targets only a single permanent or player': the target is a spell. Refused (restricted) either way.

control,scope.label: grammar right
control,scope.why: 'a token that's a copy of target creature you control': control and target belong to the ORIGINAL. The token copies only copiable values (CR 707.2) and is its creator's (CR 111.2); parseSubject read 'you control' and 'target' as the token's. The copiable values the original states (a chosen type, a keyword) are kept, so 'each creature you control of the chosen type' and '... with haste' land here too.

other,scope.label: grammar right
other,scope.why: 'a creature other than this creature': singular, so no mass scope; parseSubject's scope reads the word 'other' as a class-minus-this. The grammar says `other`, which is what the words mean.

keyword.label: grammar right
keyword.why: 'a spell that has convoke', 'another spell that has flash': the keyword the spell has, the same demand as 'a spell with convoke'. parseSubject reads keywords only after 'with'.

other,scope,type.label: grammar right
other,scope,type.why: 'a permanent other than this enchantment': the subject is a permanent; 'enchantment' names THIS card. parseSubject took the type from the exclusion.

combat,scope.label: grammar right
combat,scope.why: 'a token that's a copy of another target attacking creature': attacking is not a copiable value; the token is not attacking and not targeted.

notType,other,type.label: grammar right
notType,other,type.why: 'target nonland permanent other than this creature': a nonland permanent, not this one; parseSubject took 'creature' from the exclusion and dropped the negation.

other,subtype.label: grammar right
other,subtype.why: 'all permanents other than this Equipment': the subtype names this card, not the class.

other,type.label: grammar right
other,type.why: 'Dinosaurs you control other than this creature', 'target permanent other than this creature': the type names this card, not the class.

scope,token.label: grammar right
scope,token.why: 'a token that's a copy of target nontoken creature': the copy IS a token; 'nontoken' describes the original. parseSubject read the token as nontoken.

tapped.label: grammar right
tapped.why: 'target tapped creature', 'an untapped creature you control', 'a tapped Treasure token': a status the schema now holds (`tapped`); parseSubject dropped the word, so the filter claimed every creature. An OR whose alternatives disagree on it ('target artifact or tapped creature') is refused.

notColors.label: grammar right
notColors.why: 'target nonblack creature' (Doom Blade family), 'target nonwhite, nonblack creature': negated colours (`notColors`); parseSubject dropped them. 'nonartifact, nonblack' keeps only the colour, as parseSubject keeps no negation that removes nothing from 'creature'.

targets,type.label: grammar right
targets,type.why: 'a spell that targets this creature' (owner 2026-10-01: the trigger condition is being targeted by a spell): the subject is the SPELL and `targets` holds what it targets. parseSubject made the subject the targeted creature. eventMatches refuses `targets` until a producer can state it.

colorCount.label: grammar right
colorCount.why: 'a multicolored spell', 'target monocolored creature' (`colorCount`); parseSubject dropped the word.

basic.label: grammar right
basic.why: 'target nonbasic land' (`basic: false`); parseSubject dropped it, so the filter claimed basics too.

snow.label: grammar right
snow.why: 'a snow land', 'Snow creatures you control' (`snow`); parseSubject had no field.

legendary.label: grammar right
legendary.why: 'target nonlegendary creature' (`legendary: false`); parseSubject dropped the negation.

hasCounter.label: grammar right
hasCounter.why: 'a creature you control with a counter on it' (`hasCounter`): some counter, kind unstated; parseSubject read nothing.

targets.label: grammar right
targets.why: 'a spell that targets ~', 'target spell that targets you': `targets` holds the card itself or a player.

control,targets,type.label: grammar right
control,targets,type.why: 'a spell that targets a creature you control': 'you control' belongs to the target, not the spell.

scope,targets,type.label: grammar right
scope,targets,type.why: 'Spells your opponents cast that target this creature', 'a spell that targets one or more creatures': the targeted class sits in `targets`; the spells are the mass subject.

scope,tapped.label: grammar right
scope,tapped.why: 'each tapped creature target player controls': the player is the target; 'a tapped and attacking token that's a copy of ...': the token is created tapped, the original is targeted.

control,scope,targets,type.label: grammar right
control,scope,targets,type.why: 'Spells you cast that target a creature': the caster controls the spell; the creature is its target.

control,targets,type,umbrella.label: grammar right
control,targets,type,umbrella.why: 'target spell that targets a permanent you control': the permanent is the target.

control,targets.label: grammar right
control,targets.why: 'target instant or Aura spell that targets a permanent you control': the permanent is the target.

fromZone,snow.label: grammar right
fromZone,snow.why: 'snow lands from the top of your library': snow, from the library.

notColors,tapped.label: grammar right
notColors,tapped.why: 'target tapped nonblack creature': both narrowings, both held.

scope,targets,type,umbrella.label: grammar right
scope,targets,type,umbrella.why: 'a spell that targets one or more permanents': the count and the umbrella belong to the targets.

commander,scope,targets.label: grammar right
commander,scope,targets.why: 'Spells your opponents cast that target one or more commanders you control': the commander is the target.

control,legendary.label: grammar right
control,legendary.why: 'a token that's a copy of a nonlegendary enchantment you control': nonlegendary is copiable and kept; control is the original's.

control,modified,targets,type,umbrella.label: grammar right
control,modified,targets,type,umbrella.why: 'an Aura spell that targets a modified permanent you control': the modified permanent is the target.

control,scope,tapped.label: grammar right
control,scope,tapped.why: 'a tapped and attacking token that's a copy of target creature you control': control and target are the original's.

control,scope,tapped,token.label: grammar right
control,scope,tapped,token.why: copy of 'up to one other target nontoken creature': the copy is a token, tapped.

counter,scope,tapped.label: grammar right
counter,scope,tapped.why: 'a tapped and attacking token that's a copy of each creature card you own in exile with a memory counter on it': the counter and 'each' describe the originals.

fromZone,legendary,scope.label: grammar right
fromZone,legendary,scope.why: 'a nonlegendary, nonland card from target opponent's hand': comma-joined adjectives are one card's; the opponent is the target.

legendary,zone.label: grammar right
legendary,zone.why: 'a nonlegendary creature card in your graveyard': both held.

scope,subtype,targets.label: grammar right
scope,subtype,targets.why: 'Spells your opponents cast that target a Merfolk you control': the Merfolk is the target.

scope,targets.label: grammar right
scope,targets.why: 'Spells your opponents cast that target ~': the card itself is the target.

scope,type.label: grammar right
scope,type.why: 'a spell that targets only a single creature other than ~': restricted either way; the subject is a spell.
